high_consensus.description: Canonical status computation would silently ignore the documented blocker_risk field and miss a FAILED condition. This is high-impact, low-cost, and affects every downstream consumer that trusts the canonical verdict.

The break-glass audit_event_id ordering contradiction can make the workflow impossible to satisfy cleanly and invites manual bypasses. Clarifying the two-step emit-then-patch flow is important and cheap.
The ModelHealth pseudo-code is incomplete enough to produce direct implementation failures. The fix is straightforward, though the blast radius is narrower than the canonical verdict bug.

The cross-chunk second-stage overflow case is plausible and currently underspecified. A deterministic degraded fallback would improve reliability, though the exact truncation policy needs careful design.

If primitive_id validation is strict, KFAL audit emission could fail immediately. The uncertainty lowers the score slightly, but clarifying or registering the primitive before implementation is prudent and cheap.

disputed.description: A startup warning for a removed rollback flag is low-cost and prevents silent operator misunderstanding during migration. It is not core correctness, but the risk-reduction per effort is strong.
Specifying matrix parallelism would make the CI wall-time claim more credible, but this is mostly planning precision unless the suite is already timing out. Useful to add, but not urgent.

blockers.concern: The canonical verdict classifier is internally inconsistent with the schema and classification contract.
blockers.why_matters: Section 3.2.2 says high blocker_risk must force FAILED and consumers must trust status, but the helper in 4.4 checks a non-schema field blocker_class, never promotes high blocker_risk to FAILED, and can emit APPROVED despite schema/contract mismatch if fixtures are incomplete. This is the core safety mechanism of the cycle.
blockers.recommendation: Make §4.4 match §3.2.2 exactly, validate the computed status against the full envelope before emission, and add explicit fixtures for high, med, unknown, empty voices_dropped, and impossible count combinations.

blockers.concern: The document mixes PRD versions and source paths, creating a risk that implementation targets stale requirements.
blockers.why_matters: The header cites PRD v1.2, pre-flight says grimoires/loa/prd.md v1.1, and the changelog says v1.1. A substrate-hardening cycle gated by precise acceptance criteria can pass review while implementing the wrong revision.
blockers.recommendation: Declare one authoritative PRD path and version, include the PRD hash, and update all references before sprint planning.
